correctness.rationale: The linear rescaling 4||(. )||²=5x²+2|xy|+y² transforms to M(s,t)²=s²+t²+2c|st|, c=1/sqrt5. On each smooth quadrant, Birkhoff directions are proportional to w_z=(-(z+c),1+cz), normalized by B(z)=8(5z²+4sqrt5 z+5)/25. Euclidean distance lower-bounds M-distance, and independent exact algebra gives A(z)²-(5/8)B(z)(1+z²)=4z²/5≥0. At axis x=e1, all Birkhoff directions satisfy |r|≤c, y=(r,1)/sqrt(1+r²+2c|r|); the distance lower bound is sqrt(5/8), attained when r=c by an explicit translate to the vertical axis. Signed-permutation symmetry covers all axes and smooth points. The proof does not depend on numerical sampling.
residual_risks: Real, n=2, p=2 only; does not apply to higher Cesaro sequence spaces.

value.rationale: PASS: The finite-dimensional Cesaro plane is explicitly singled out in published Banach geometry as a canonical naturally occurring sequence-norm model. Its exact optimal reverse-Birkhoff distance distinguishes asymmetric orthogonality from James-type symmetric chords; the value sqrt(5/8) and extremal axis cone are not implied by the known J. A future comparison of approximate-orthogonality quality across sequence norms could need this precise value. No all-dimensional extension is claimed.
